touches.text: Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.

A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, "because even the basic laws rest finally upon those core principles" (Akien 2026-11-13). Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).
proof_coverage: joins a ticket's falsifier clauses to the proofs that cover them and the seals that ran green. WHY: a falsifier nobody proves is a hypothesis (Law 3). USERS: the tester.

conflicts.why: Outline 9.4.2.3.7.6 requires 'A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).' In a hollow run where ground_loop code is removed, the proof file and its sys.path.insert line remain unchanged. The tooth checks import-path correctness, which doesn't depend on ground_loop's existence. Therefore the tooth can pass in a hollow run (if parents[6] is correctly set) without verifying ground_loop's behavior, violating Law 8.
